title: The timber faller
logline: Tuesday. Page nine of the serious book, drawn across four panels of the strip: a man with a saw on a ridge, the trees, the cross-hatching. The strip lets the phantom novel onto the page once, whole, before it's buried.

panels.composition: Page nine, as drawn: a timber faller on a ridge at dawn, a saw on his shoulder, Sitka spruce, dense cross-hatching, no joke, no balloon. The strip's line for one strip is the novel's line.

image.prompt: dense cross-hatched pen-and-ink in a serious graphic-novel style, a timber faller with a saw over his shoulder on a forested ridge at dawn, no words
image.notes: This strip is the phantom novel's page 9, verbatim. Not the strip's line: crosshatch, weight, no gag. The only time it surfaces whole.

panels.composition: The faller at a trunk. The saw's first bite. Chips.

image.prompt: dense cross-hatched pen-and-ink, a man setting a saw into the base of a huge spruce, chips flying, no words

panels.composition: His face. The strip's Wood, aged fifty, in a mill jacket — the reader who knows will see it; the strip doesn't say.

image.prompt: dense cross-hatched pen-and-ink, close-up of a fifty-year-old man's weathered face under a hard hat, concentrating, no words
image.notes: The faller has Wood's face aged fifty. Reserved whether the novel is about the father.

panels.composition: The tree going over. The ridge. Above it, in the sky, where the strip would put nothing: a faint warmth in the hatching. The novel has the glow too.
props: a faint glow in the hatching

image.prompt: dense cross-hatched pen-and-ink, a huge spruce falling on a ridge with a faint warm lightness worked into the hatching of the sky above, no words
image.notes: The glow, in the novel's hatching, 2006. Before 'Lanes.'

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind

notes: The phantom novel surfaces whole, once. The faller has his face at fifty. The glow is in the hatching.
